title: MRI Project Spinoza REC Preparation Protocol
author: Tinka Beemsterboer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2bvgan6
materials: Decide on whether to use additional stimulus equipment. Note: users are not allowed to change the stimulus set-up of the Spinoza Centre REC without approval from Spinoza staff. If you think additional stimulus equipment or other programs are necessary for your experiment, please let us know. For example: Auditory stimuli; PPU (cardiac signal) and respiratory belt. This is free of charge and it is not necessary to book extra time for this; Eye tracker; EEG; Skin conductance; EMG; Electro-stimulator device (pain stimulation) TMS Ideally, mention if you plan on using extra stimulus equipment during the introduction meeting. For the use of additional equipment additional training is required. This is mostly done in short courses, depending on the experience of the user. The user may very well be an experienced user already, in this case we only verify correct handling of the equipment and some MRI specifics. This “exam” can be done within an hour and there are no additional costs. To get experience using the equipment you may consider consulting an experienced fellow researcher. There are no additional costs for using GSR, EMG, EyeTracker, Electrical stimulation, ECG, PPU, Resperatory belt and auditory system. Electrodes and other accessories are provided and also without additional costs. The additional costs for the use of EEG are 50/hr if you need to use a cap from the Spinoza Center. For TMS this still needs to be determined, contact Steven Scholte for more information. We are happy to give you advice and/or more information about the additional equipment.

Estimate the time needed for one participant. Below you find an approximation of the scan time needed per participant depending on the stimulus setup; note that the duration of the scans should include communication to the participant, set up of the scans, shimming and survey scan. Furthermore the time needed per participant is dependent on the type of participants and the experience of the researcher. Simple protocol, possibly including PPU and Resp: duration of the scans + 10 minutes; With GSR or EMG measurements: duration of the scans + 20 minutes; With eye tracker measurements: duration of the scans + 20 minutes. Of course, this estimation may be adjusted after the pilot or during your experiment.

steps.title: Create Calpendo user accounts
steps.instruction: All project members (PI, researchers, assistants, interns) must obtain a Calpendo account at https://spinozarec.calpendo.com, the system used for MRI bookings, safety, and equipment certifications.

steps.title: Create project in Calpendo
steps.instruction: After user accounts are approved, the PI creates a new project: press Projects → Create Project, enter the unique short project code, upload the Ethics Committee‑approved protocol, specify resources (hours and cost per hour for the MRI scanner), add all users who may manage bookings, set Safety = true for any stimulus equipment, and note that certificates are required for Eyetracker, TMS, EGI and electrical stimulator (contact Tinka Beemsterboer for certification details).

steps.title: Complete user agreement and contract
steps.instruction: The PI signs the Calpendo User Agreement; the budget holder signs the project contract (file: scanovereenkomstrecl_eng_v2.4.pdf) and sends the signed contract to t.beemsterboer@uva.nl. If pricing details are missing, contact Tinka Beemsterboer or Steven Scholte before signing.

steps.title: Notify Tinka of requested project and equipment
steps.instruction: Email Tinka Beemsterboer (t.beemsterboer@uva.nl) after the Calpendo project request, stating which stimulus equipment (as set in the Safety tab) will be used.

steps.title: Request storage folder access
steps.instruction: Obtain access to an export folder on the data‑server: UvA FMG researchers use an ‘fMRI Projects’ folder, external researchers use a ‘Dropbox’ folder. Follow the provided links for UvA FMG or external access and the FTP‑server instructions.

steps.title: Verify paradigm waits for scanner trigger
steps.instruction: Ensure the experimental paradigm does not start until it receives the first keyboard ‘t’ response, which is sent by the scanner at the start of each BOLD volume (excluding dummy scans). The paradigm must wait for this first ‘t’ before proceeding. Supported stimulus programs on the stimulus computer are Presentation, E‑Prime, Matlab (Psychtoolbox) and PsychoPy; contact Tinka for other programs.

steps.title: Confirm button box and peripheral mapping
steps.instruction: Check that the experiment correctly maps the response buttons of the MRI‑compatible button boxes to the expected keyboard responses (e.g., left index finger → ‘e’). If you wish to use the MRI‑compatible mouse or joystick, inform the centre in advance.

steps.title: Select scan sequences and calculate duration
steps.instruction: Decide which scan sequences to run (structural T1‑weighted, T2‑weighted; functional EPI; diffusion DWI; field‑map B0 or top‑up). Estimate the total scan time and ensure it matches the length of your behavioural paradigm. Notify the centre early if you need non‑standard sequences.

steps.title: Obtain ethical committee approval
steps.instruction: First obtain approval from an ethical committee. Email lab-fmg@uva.nl and t.beemsterboer@uva.nl requesting an account on the EC website (https://www.lab.uva.nl/lab). After receiving the account, log in, click ‘Onderzoeker’ in the upper right corner, and follow the on‑screen instructions to submit your EC application.

steps.title: Prepare participant screening and consent documents
steps.instruction:
Gather the following documents for the EC application and for participants: 
- Information letter & informed consent (fMRI_InformationLetterAndInformedConsent_sep2018.docx, adapt as needed) 
- GP informed consent (InformedConsentMRI_GP_SpinozaREC_EN_v2.pdf, InformedConsentMRI_GP_SpinozaREC_NL_v2.pdf) 
- Screening forms (ScreeningMRI_SpinozaREC_EN_V10.pdf, ScreeningMRI_SpinozaREC_NL_V10.pdf) 
- MRI‑research information brochure (Spinoza_REC_MRI_info_EN_V7.pdf, Spinoza_REC_MRI_info_NL_V7.pdf) 
- Description of anomaly (incidental findings) procedure (DescriptionAnomalyProcedure_SpinozaREC_v2016.pdf). Include all files in the EC submission.

steps.title: Conduct pilot session with experienced subject
steps.instruction: Schedule a pilot scan with an experienced participant by emailing Tinka Beemsterboer. Review the “Protocol on running an MRI pilot at Spinoza REC” checklist before the session and contact Tinka with any questions.

steps.title: Choose preprocessing and QC pipelines
steps.instruction: Decide whether to use the centre’s automatic BIDS conversion, preprocessing (fMRIPrep) and quality‑control (MRIQC) pipelines. Note that the BIDS‑conversion tool (bidsify) works only with standard sequences and cannot handle scans that are manually stopped; correct naming of scans is the researcher’s responsibility.

steps.title: Organize exported data in BIDS folder structure
steps.instruction: Export raw scanner data to a subfolder named ‘raw’ inside your export folder (fMRI Projects or Dropbox). Create a subject folder (e.g., sub‑01) and, if applicable, a session folder (e.g., ses‑01). Name files according to the BIDS convention (e.g., sub‑01_ses‑01_T1w.PAR). You cannot create directories from the scan‑computer; use the ‘scan‑assistant’ computer for that. After ~24 h the centre will copy the data, run BIDS conversion, and place results in a ‘bids’ directory with sub‑folders ‘anat’, ‘dwi’, ‘fmap’, ‘func’, and a ‘derivatives’ folder containing fmriprep, freesurfer and mriqc outputs (HTML reports).

substeps.instruction: Do not create additional directories on the scan‑computer; use the scan‑assistant computer if needed
After processing, find converted data in <ExportFolder>/raw/bids/ and derivatives in <ExportFolder>/raw/derivatives/

steps.title: Ensure liability and personal insurance coverage
steps.instruction: Confirm that the University of Amsterdam liability insurance (deductible €25 000) covers non‑invasive MRI research for you and your participants. If the Medical Research Act (WMO) applies, obtain separate insurance. The centre also recommends that each user holds personal liability insurance.

steps.title: Screen participants and submit screening forms
steps.instruction: Pre‑screen all participants using the MRI‑safety screening form (consult the radiology department‑provided questionnaire). The MR‑operator has final responsibility for safety. After each scan session, deposit the completed MR‑screening form in the mailbox located in the MR‑operator room.

steps.title: Review Lab Guide and regulations
steps.instruction: Read the Lab Guide (access via https://top.socsci.uva.nl/?page_id=1793 with your UvAnetID) for information on data storage, participant reimbursement, and material procurement. Skip the section on booking projects. The technical support website is https://top.socsci.uva.nl/.

steps.title: Plan data sharing in EC application
steps.instruction: If you intend to share anonymised data, state this in the EC application. Use the template information letter (see step 10) which contains a paragraph permitting data sharing. When the centre’s preprocessing/QC pipeline is used, the data will be formatted for upload to the OpenNeuro repository.

steps.title: Note centre’s daily data processing at 11 pm
steps.instruction: Every day at 11 pm the centre checks the export folders (fMRI Projects or Dropbox) for new data, copies them to the server, and starts BIDS conversion, QC, and optional preprocessing.

steps.title: Be aware of weekly and monthly scanner QC
steps.instruction: The centre performs weekly quality checks (quick system check, phantom scan, stimulus verification) and monthly recalibrations (including 32‑channel head‑coil diagnostics). Any irregularities that may affect previous scans will be communicated to you.

steps.title: Subscribe to Spinoza REC mailing list
steps.instruction: Send an email to t.beemsterboer@uva.nl requesting to be added to the mailing list. The list can later be accessed at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/uva3tmri.

steps.title: Arrange participant monetary rewards or RC credits
steps.instruction: Organise monetary compensation within your research group. For UvA Psychology students, arrange RC credits by contacting Tinka Beemsterboer.
